brief: Goldman Sachs FICC and Equities sales recap of day three of the Communacopia and Technology Conference. It reports management remarks rather than arguing a house view. Nvidia's Huang put AI's addressable market at $3tn-$4tn by 2030 on the shift from retrieval-based to generative computing, said slowing Moore's Law raises the value of the integrated hardware, software and networking stack and lets Nvidia take a growing share of AI capex, and reaffirmed about 70% year-over-year growth in CY27 despite packaging, memory, power and datacentre constraints. SpaceX's CFO tied confidence in a $100bn annualised revenue run-rate by year-end 2026 to a signed $1.11bn per month hosting agreement starting in December and compute monetised at $30-50bn per GW, with just over 2GW of capacity by YE26 and 5-10GW by YE27, power the binding long-term constraint. Uber, CrowdStrike, Datadog, Palo Alto, MongoDB, Intuit and Mastercard each framed AI adoption as a demand driver rather than a cost, each with company metrics attached. Mastercard reported consumer and business spending strong through August.
